region.text: Transjordan, the land east of the Jordan

ledger.note: 11 April 1921: the Emirate of Transjordan is established with Abdullah as emir at Amman. Infobox 'Established 11 April 1921', capital Amman; Abdullah was 'moving to Amman on 2 March 1921'; the Jordan page: 'Transjordan remained a British mandate until 1946'. The page names the land (Transjordan) but gives no boundary; the Aqaba and Ma'an districts are added in 1925.

region.text: the Aqaba and Ma'an districts of the Hejaz

ledger.note: May 1925: Aqaba and Ma'an pass to Transjordan. 'In May 1925, Ibn Saud gave up the Aqaba and Ma'an districts of the Hejaz.' The page names the recipient: 'and it became part of British Emirate of Transjordan'; the Emirate page links the area to the 1924-25 Saudi conquest of the Hejaz and shows it in Transjordan afterwards (Ibn Saud later respected the Ma'an position privately in the 1927 Treaty of Jeddah).

25 May 1946: Transjordan becomes the Hashemite Kingdom of Transjordan. 'On 25 May 1946 the Transjordan became the Hashemite Kingdom of Transjordan'; the Treaty of London was signed 'on 22 March 1946' and full independence came on 17 June 1946 when ratifications were exchanged. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: 15 May 1948: Jordan intervenes in the Palestine war. 'On 15 May 1948, as part of the 1948 Palestine war, Jordan intervened along with several other Arab states'; the 1948 War page: the Arab Legion 'fought only in the area that King Abdullah wanted to secure for Jordan: the West Bank, including East Jerusalem'.

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: May 1948: the Arab Legion holds the West Bank. The Legion fought in 'the West Bank, including East Jerusalem'; the Jordan page: 'Following the war, Jordan controlled the West Bank, and on 24 April 1950 Jordan formally annexed these territories.' Hatched over the Palestinians until the annexation; at the Jericho Conference of 1 December 1948 '2,000 Palestinian delegates supported a resolution calling for the unification of Palestine and Transjordan' (Palestinians page, read for the palestinians dossier).

1949: the Hashemite Kingdom of Transjordan becomes the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in English. The page says it 'continued to be referred to as the Hashemite Kingdom of Transjordan in English until 1949'; the Arabic name already read 'Jordan' from 1946. [Reviewer me-10-j, 2026-10-25: the annexation page dates it: 'Transjordan became the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan on 26 April 1949'.]

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: 3 April 1949: Jordan and Israel sign the armistice. 'On 3 April 1949, Israel and Jordan signed an armistice agreement'; 'Jordanian forces remained in most positions they held in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem and the Old City'.

'Israel received control in the area known as Wadi Ara' and the Little Triangle in the Jordan agreement, 'in exchange for territory in the southern hills of Hebron'. No boundary on the page; the regions are the researcher's reading. [Reviewer me-10-j, 2026-10-25: region clipped to the side of the armistice line it lies on; the bare radius took in land on both sides.]

region.text: territory in the southern hills of Hebron

'The West Bank was formally annexed on 24 April 1950'; 'Recognition ... was granted only by the United Kingdom, Iraq, and possibly Pakistan'; the annexation 'more than tripled' the population (400,000 to 1,300,000). The Gaza Strip stayed under Egypt.

notes: Written by me-10-j from nine pages (the page budget). SCOPE: the dossier starts in 1921 (the Emirate of Transjordan, same state and dynasty, rename 1946 and 1949) because Cliopatria has no row for 1921-1946; the Cliopatria shapes begin in 1947. WEST BANK: Cliopatria gives it to Jordan from 1949 and to Israel from 1967; the dossier has the Arab Legion hold it over the Palestinians from May 1948 (occupation, hatched), the formal annexation on 24 April 1950, the Israeli occupation from June 1967 and Jordan's renunciation on 31 July 1988; the palestinians dossier (1948-1950) is the owner row for 1948-1950. ARAB FEDERATION: Cliopatria draws the federation shape for 1958-1959 and has no Jordan shape for those years; the federation lasted 14 February to 2 August 1958 only (new keyframe for 1959). 1965 EXCHANGE: the page's figures (+6,000 km2 interior, 19 km of coast, -7,000 km2) do not reproduce the shape drop between 1960 and 1967 (about 7,700 km2 on the East Bank, gain about 760 km2 by cells); the ledger regions are the cell differences. Naharayim coordinates are the researcher's. NOT READ (page budget): British Mandate and the 1922-1928 Transjordan agreements (British vassal events belong to the kingdom-of-great-britain dossier: 15 May 1923 'Britain recognised Transjordan as an independent government', 20 February 1928 agreement), Black September, the Hebron-hills exchange boundary, the 27 June 1967 Israeli extension of law to East Jerusalem (in the state-of-israel dossier). Unexplained small steps: 1953 (+233 km2), 1956 (-233 km2). Region names the gazetteer lacks: Wadi Ara, Little Triangle, Naharayim (coordinates used).
